questions.q: Which four ordinary questions does the chapter say can determine whether a retreat happens at all?
options: When, where, for how long, and what to do with the phone
questions.explanation: Many people who want unhurried time with God never create it because they never settle the ordinary questions. A retreat does not need to be elaborate; it needs to be protected.

questions.q: What does the chapter say about a retreat you can protect versus one that sounds impressive?
options: Always choose the longest possible retreat
Anything shorter than three days is a waste of time
A one-day retreat that happens is worth more than a three-day retreat that stays on your list for a year
questions.explanation: Choose the length you can actually protect. Extended solitude is not automatically better, and going longer than three days deserves guidance from someone experienced.

questions.q: According to the location table, which setting is described as best suited to a first three-day retreat?
questions.explanation: Retreat centres and religious communities are purpose-built for silence, so the environment does much of the protecting for you, if it is within your means.

questions.q: Which location does the chapter call the hardest option, and how does it work best?
options: A hotel, because of the television
Home with the household present, using the at-home format with sessions early or late and other adults protecting the time
A borrowed home, because of privacy
questions.explanation: Many parents and caregivers will have to use it. Be realistic, you will be interrupted, and Chapter 3 told you what to do about that.

questions.q: What is the chapter's advice about connectivity in a location?
options: Go somewhere with no signal at all
Keep the phone on and check it hourly
Reliable reception with the phone silenced may be safer than no signal; keep emergency calling available where possible
questions.explanation: Solitude does not require placing yourself beyond the reach of help. The digital boundary in Chapter 9 handles the rest.

questions.q: Which elements of a retreat does the chapter say are free?
options: Unhurried time, honesty before God, Scripture and silence
questions.explanation: Some readers will not go because they cannot afford a retreat centre. That is exactly the situation the book addresses: the most important elements cost nothing, everything else is helpful but optional.

reflection: Length: three days, one day, three hours, or an eight-day at-home retreat. If three days, which three?
Location: which of the options above, and specifically where? If you need to ask someone, write down whom and when you will ask.
The seven questions: go through them for your chosen place. Any that you answered "no" to need a solution or a different place.
Dates: the retreat itself, plus a softer day before and after if you can arrange it.
